about: What the prefill chunk derivation (roofline/chunk_size.py) reads beyond a model's header and the chip's peaks: per engine, how it stages the experts of layers kept in RAM (cache_copy: a cached expert is copied device to device into a scratch tensor before its GEMM; copy_calls: host calls per reached expert per expert tensor; serial: the staging runs between the GPU's kernels, not beside them); and measured rows of one setup, keyed by the model and draft (header ids, roofline/routing_profile.identity), target, engine, context, KV type and the build's features (switches compiled in; a row applies to a build that has them all, the most specific wins). A row may hold: staging (its build's own staging row), the experts a chunk reaches, the expert cache's hit share at a layout, copy rates and per-call cost, used memory at load per chunk (load probes or timed arms), the margin's terms (free at load and lowest free over a session: tune.session_margin), the non-expert rows a loaded run held at held_at (each [MiB, label]), measured layouts (a timed arm per chunk) and quality gates per chunk (result passed or failed). Elsewhere every figure is derived or an estimate, labelled.

llama.cpp.why: ggml-cuda copy_experts stages every expert a chunk reaches of a layer kept in RAM into a scratch tensor, one copy per expert tensor, from the expert cache (device to device) or host RAM (upload), issued by the host between the layer's kernels (the GPU waits)
llama.cpp.evidence: boltbeam-runs/prefill-audit-128k-20261115 sections 2-4: 7,781 device copies + 291 uploads per 128-token chunk, 168 experts x 48 layer-tensors, GPU idle 20.7 ms a chunk at the splits
